app.title: folio-lab
app.tagline: Backtest portfolios that mix Thai funds, Thai stocks, and global ETFs in one place
app.disclaimer: Past performance does not guarantee future returns. Nothing here is investment advice.

notice.rangeClamped: The period was adjusted to {start} to {end} based on the data available for {symbol}
notice.converted: All figures are shown in {currency}, converted at each month's exchange rate
notice.inflationOn: Figures marked after inflation show buying power compared with the start of the period, using Thai inflation
notice.inflationGap: Inflation for {years} has not been published yet, so those years are not adjusted. Every other year is
notice.twoReturns: The table shows two kinds of return: the portfolio return measures the assets alone and ignores when you added money, while the return on your money counts the timing of every deposit and withdrawal.
notice.allocationTarget: A portfolio that spreads added money by target weights pulls its weights back to target along the way, so its portfolio return no longer compares directly with the others.
notice.portfolioDepleted: This portfolio ran out in {month}, so its value is zero from then on.
notice.rollingWindowTooLong: The period you chose is shorter than {window}, so there is nothing to show yet.

startAmount.label: Starting amount
startAmount.hint: The amount assumed to be invested at the start of the period

endBalance.label: Ending balance
endBalance.hint: What the starting amount grows into by the end of the selected period

cagr.label: Annualised return
cagr.hint: The average yearly growth rate that would produce the same result if it were identical every year. Higher is better

stdev.label: Annualised volatility
stdev.hint: How far returns swing from their average. Higher means a bumpier ride

bestYear.label: Best year
bestYear.hint: The best calendar year in the period, counting full years only

worstYear.label: Worst year
worstYear.hint: The worst calendar year in the period, counting full years only. It shows how much a bad year hurts

maxDrawdown.label: Maximum drawdown
maxDrawdown.hint: The deepest fall from a previous peak before recovering to that peak

sharpe.label: Sharpe
sharpe.hint: Return earned above a risk-free deposit per unit of volatility. Higher means better paid for the risk

sortino.label: Sortino
sortino.hint: Like Sharpe, but it only penalises downward swings. Useful if losses worry you more than bumpiness

totalContributed.label: Total contributed
totalContributed.hint: The starting amount plus every deposit, which is the money that actually left your pocket.

totalWithdrawn.label: Total withdrawn
totalWithdrawn.hint: Everything actually withdrawn across all periods. A portfolio set to withdraw shows this instead of total contributed.

moneyWeightedReturn.label: Return on your money
moneyWeightedReturn.hint: How fast the money you put in grew per year, counting when you added or withdrew it. The portfolio return ignores that timing.

rebalanceCount.label: Times rebalanced
rebalanceCount.hint: How many times you would have had to pull the weights back over the period. This figure ignores fees and taxes.

rollingReturn.label: Rolling return
rollingReturn.hint: If you had started in any month and held for the full stretch, where the result lands. It shows how much the outcome depends on timing.

rollingAverage.label: Average across starting points
rollingAverage.hint: The average of every starting point for that stretch, not the compound return of the whole period. These are different numbers.

positiveWindowShare.label: Share that made a gain
positiveWindowShare.hint: Out of every possible starting point, the percentage that ended in a gain after holding the full stretch.

beta.label: Beta
beta.hint: How many units this portfolio moves when the market moves one. Below one means it swings less than the market.

alpha.label: Alpha (per year)
alpha.hint: How much better or worse it did than expected for the risk taken, stated per year.

rSquared.label: Market alignment
rSquared.hint: How much of the portfolio's movement is explained by the market. Higher means it tracks the market more closely.

trackingError.label: Gap from the market (per year)
trackingError.hint: How unpredictably this portfolio drifts away from the market. Higher means less market-like.

informationRatio.label: Return per unit of gap
informationRatio.hint: For the ground it covered away from the market, was the return worth the added uncertainty?

upsideCapture.label: Following the market up
upsideCapture.hint: In months when the market rose, how much of that rise this portfolio captured.

downsideCapture.label: Following the market down
downsideCapture.hint: In months when the market fell, how much of that fall this portfolio took. Lower means it holds up better.

varHistorical.label: The worst 5% of months beat this
varHistorical.hint: Of all months so far, 5% lost more than this figure.

varAnalytical.label: The worst 5% of months (statistical)
varAnalytical.hint: The same figure derived from the shape of the distribution rather than counting actual months, useful for comparing the two.

cvar.label: Average of the worst 5% of months
cvar.hint: When those bad months do arrive, how much they lose on average. Answers how deep, not just how often.

skewness.label: Skew
skewness.hint: Which way returns lean. Negative means bad months tend to be worse than good months are good.

kurtosis.label: Tail thickness
kurtosis.hint: How often extreme months show up compared with normal. High means violent months happen more than expected.

calmar.label: Return per unit of pain
calmar.hint: Annual return against the deepest loss ever endured. Higher means return without having to stomach as much.

riskContribution.label: Risk share
riskContribution.hint: How much of the portfolio's swing comes from this holding, which differs from the money weight. Negative means it dampens the swing.

returnContribution.label: Profit share
returnContribution.hint: How much of the portfolio's total profit came from this holding.

contributionAmount.label: Profit in money
contributionAmount.hint: That profit share expressed in money. All holdings together equal the portfolio's profit.

correlation.label: How closely they move together
correlation.hint: How much these two move the same way. Near one is almost identical, near zero is unrelated.

summary.heading: Backtest summary
summary.noDownside: Cannot be calculated because there are no losing months
summary.noMoneyWeighted: No rate fits this pattern of money in and out.

chart.nominalNote: This line is still in nominal terms. It is not adjusted for inflation, because the available inflation rates are yearly and not detailed enough for a monthly chart.
chart.logDisabledHint: Log scale is unavailable because this period includes zero or negative values
chart.viewAsTable: View as a table of year-end values
chart.chartAlt: Everything in this chart is available in the accompanying table
chart.yearEndCaption: Portfolio and market value at each year end

drawdown.heading: Drawdowns and recovery
drawdown.chartCaption: How far below the previous peak the portfolio was, month by month
drawdown.found: {count} drawdowns in total, showing the {shown} deepest
drawdown.none: No drawdowns in the selected period. The portfolio never fell below a previous peak

rolling.heading: Rolling returns
rolling.intro: If you had started in any month and held for the full stretch, where would the result land?
rolling.pureNote: This section uses the portfolio return alone. It ignores money added or withdrawn and is not inflation-adjusted.
rolling.chartCaption: The lowest-to-highest range for each holding period, with a tick at the average
rolling.chartAlt: Each bar spans the lowest to the highest return for that holding period, and the tick across it marks the average. Every value is also in the table below.
rolling.averageWarning: Average means the average across every starting point, not the compound return of the whole period. These are different numbers.

monthly.heading: Monthly returns
monthly.pureNote: These are the portfolio returns alone. They ignore money added or withdrawn and are not inflation-adjusted.
monthly.saveHint: Save the monthly returns table as a file you can open in a spreadsheet

share.manualHint: Your browser would not copy it automatically. Select the whole thing and copy it.

correlation.heading: How closely your holdings move together
correlation.intro: A number near 1 means these two move the same way almost all the time, so holding both barely spreads your risk. Near 0 means they go their own ways.
correlation.caption: Correlation between the holdings of {name}

decomposition.heading: What you put in vs. the risk you actually carry
decomposition.intro: Weight is how much money you put in. Risk share is where the portfolio's swings come from. They are not the same, and the ones that differ most are the ones worth a look.
decomposition.negativeNote: A negative figure in the risk column is a good thing: that holding offsets some of the swing from the others.
decomposition.caption: Return and risk breakdown for {name}
